result.note: Mainly a corporate CEO appointment; tested only the durable ownership structure, the profitability record and the Pakistani airspace ban.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about Air India, as reported in August 2026:
items: Tata Sons own about 75 per cent of Air India, with Singapore Airlines holding the rest.
Air India has turned a profit in every year since Tata regained control in 2022.
Since April 2025, Pakistan has barred Indian carriers from its airspace.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Air India has not turned a profit since Tata regained control in 2022. Air India Group posted a record loss of more than USD 2 billion in fiscal 2025-26. Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran has said the turnaround could take up to a decade.
questions.source: Tata Sons own about 75 per cent of Air India, with Singapore Airlines holding the rest, and Chairman N. Chandrasekaran has said the turnaround could take up to a decade.
